Setting $\deriv{\mean}\ell = 0$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
0 &= \frac{1}{\varpar}\paren{\sumin x_i - n\mean}
&& \text{(score for $\mean$)}\\
0 &= \sumin x_i - n\mean
&& \text{(multiply both sides by $\varpar$)}\\
n\mean &= \sumin x_i
&& \text{(add $n\mean$ to both sides)}\\
\mean &= \avgin x_i
&& \text{(divide by $n$)}\\
\mean &= \bar x
&& \text{(definition of $\bar x$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

This solution does not depend on $\varpar$.
The second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mean^2}
&= \deriv{\mean}\paren{\frac{1}{\varpar}\paren{\sumin x_i - n\mean}}
&& \text{(differentiate the score for $\mean$)}\\
&= \frac{1}{\varpar}\deriv{\mean}\paren{\sumin x_i - n\mean}
&& \text{(constant multiple rule)}\\
&= \frac{1}{\varpar}\paren{\deriv{\mean}\sumin x_i - \deriv{\mean}\paren{n\mean}}
&& \text{(linearity of differentiation)}\\
&= \frac{1}{\varpar}\paren{0 - \deriv{\mean}\paren{n\mean}}
&& \text{($\textstyle\sumin x_i$ does not depend on $\mean$)}\\
&= \frac{1}{\varpar}\paren{0 - n\deriv{\mean}\mean}
&& \text{(constant multiple rule)}\\
&= \frac{1}{\varpar}\paren{0 - n}
&& \text{(derivative of $\mean$ with respect to itself)}\\
&= \frac{1}{\varpar}\paren{-n}
&& \text{(subtract)}\\
&= -\frac{n}{\varpar}
&& \text{(multiply)}\\
&< 0,
&& \text{($n > 0$ and $\varpar > 0$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

so for every fixed $\varpar$, $\ell$ is maximized over $\mean$ at $\bar x$,
and $\hmean_{\text{ML}} = \bar x$.
